synthesis: The spike asks whether an org-scoped plate-distinct (uniqExact(ocr)) read of clarity.scans_cold is affordable on the Company Metrics dashboard page-load path, gating DEV-2467/2468/2469/2470. It is: GO. Both of the ticket's stated premises are wrong, and so is the correction comment 39123. Production sorts scans_cold by (org_id, scanned_at, kit_id, id) -- org_id is the LEADING primary-key column, so an org-scoped query prunes fully by binary search (266,535 -> 1,698 granules) and cost scales with org size by ~1,900x rather than being org-independent. The kit_id-routing workaround comment 39123 recommends is 6.7x worse because kit_id is the third sort-key column. The real cost centre is not the card total (8 KB-650 MB, 8-374 ms) but the 13-month sparkline series getMonthlyData() needs, which no pre-aggregate can answer for period-distinct plates: 2.51 GB peak / 1,351 ms for the worst-case org, and ~10 GB concurrent peak across four unbatched cards. Batching, dropping FINAL, and a WITH ROLLUP shape bring that inside budget. What remains unresolved is definitional, not performance: period-distinct vs the hourly-sum the shipped affiliate report already calls 'unique scans' differ by 1.18-1.63x.

questions.q: What does 'unique scan' mean on the card -- period-distinct plates (uniqExact(ocr) over scans_cold for the window), or the hourly-sum (sum(unique_plates) over affiliate_stats_hourly) that the shipped affiliate report already calls 'unique scans'? The two differ by 1.18x-1.63x, and the factor varies by org so it cannot be corrected by a constant.
questions.answer: Period-distinct plates -- uniqExact(ocr) over the window. Answered from the ticket set and shipped code, not by preference, three independent ways: (1) DEV-2467's own AC says 'Counts distinct ocr', and an hourly-sum is not a distinct count; (2) the DEV-2406 hit-side precedent DEV-2467 is required to match is HitPlateStatsBatchQuery, which computes uniqExactIf(ocr, ...) over the window from hits_cold and explicitly rejects the rollup in its docblock because it has no plate column; (3) affiliate_stats_hourly has no ocr and no scan-id column, so DEV-2469/2470 (distinct plates among scans attributed to a repossession via recovery_scans) structurally cannot use it at any cost -- and DEV-2469's AC requires sharing the sibling unique-scan cache key, so all four cards must share one definition. Period-distinct is the only definition all four can produce. The affiliate report's looser number is a different, coarser metric; record the 1.18x-1.63x divergence in the Build Record the way DEV-2467 already requires for the Scan Count divergence.

notes: Comment 39123 (2026-09-04) states the sort key as (kit_id, scanned_at, id) and recommends routing org queries through kit_id. Production is (org_id, scanned_at, kit_id, id) and the kit_id route is 6.7x worse. The comment's core conclusion (GO, no new DDL needed) is right; its mechanism is not.

Open item 1 of comment 39123 ('server-side envelope not obtainable, readonly_user lacks READ ON REMOTE') is resolved: the X-ClickHouse-Summary HTTP response header carries read_rows / read_bytes / memory_usage / elapsed_ns with no extra grant.
Open item 2 (incomplete matrix) is resolved: full 2 orgs x 4 windows, plus a third org.

Open item 4 (rollup coverage unverified) is resolved: 264/264 Aug orgs present, 262 exact, 264 within 1%, 0 over 5% off, global ratio 1.000000. The 548-vs-386 gap is orgs owning kits that have never scanned.
Open item 3 (the definitional question) is the ONE thing still open -- it is the gate question above.
Last 7d and This Month are the SAME window on the 8th of any month (subDays(7)->startOfDay() == startOfMonth()). Not a measurement error.

FINAL is pure overhead for uniqExact(ocr): +97% server time, +149% bytes, identical answer across 3/3 runs. Verified mechanism -- 1,635 duplicate-id groups in the sample, 0 carrying more than one distinct ocr, 0 delete flips, 0 soft-deleted rows. Contrast hits_cold, where a mutable sort-key column makes FINAL load-bearing (DEV-2406).
scans_hot is NOT a win for the current-month window: 3.3x slower than scans_cold (454 ms vs 139 ms) because it carries 5x the parts, so FINAL's merge work dominates.
affiliate_stats_hourly freshness must be probed with max(_peerdb_synced_at), not max(scan_hour) -- the table holds junk scan_hour values up to 2051-05-26. Measured lag: 1 minute.
GROUP BY kit_id WITH ROLLUP serves DEV-2467's org total (kit_id = 0) and DEV-2468's per-kit leaderboard from one scan; the ROLLUP total matched the standalone scalar exactly (2,800,575).
A third definition lurks in the leaderboard: per-kit distinct plates do not sum to org distinct plates. The card must state which it shows.

RESOLVED: the definitional question. Period-distinct, established from DEV-2467's AC + HitPlateStatsBatchQuery's shipped pattern + the structural impossibility of serving DEV-2469/2470 from affiliate_stats_hourly (no ocr, no scan id).

BONUS: clarity.recovery_scans already carries ocr, so DEV-2469/2470 never need scans_cold. Measured org 1271: single window 953,806 rows / 17.0 MB / 50 MB / 493 ms; 13-month series 1,195,761 rows / 22.2 MB / 36 MB / 27 ms -- 51x fewer rows and 70x less memory than DEV-2467's scans_cold path. DEV-2469's stated data path ('needed for the plate (ocr)... resolve plates from scans_cold') is unnecessary. recovery_scans has no org_id; scope through clarity.recoveries, whose sort key (org_id, repo_date, id) leads with org_id.

A UI decision remains but does not block: whether to reconcile or explain the divergence against the existing (un-deduped) Scan Count card and the affiliate report's looser 'unique scans'. DEV-2467 already requires this be recorded explicitly.

A cold render pays one 13-month query per card; warm renders read cache.

Scan::hot() routing is inert ($scan::query() is static, discards setTable) so the current-month branch reads scans_cold anyway. Pre-existing (DEV-2324); measured here as incidentally harmless since scans_cold is in fact FASTER than scans_hot for this window.

data_impact.mv_or_cdc_implications: Read-only spike; nothing written. Relevant CDC facts measured: ocr is immutable across a scan's CDC versions (0 of 1,635 duplicate-id groups carry two plates), so FINAL is unnecessary for uniqExact(ocr). affiliate_stats_hourly is a ReplacingMergeTree fed from zod.public.aggregate_scan_count_unq_h with a measured 1-minute sync lag and junk scan_hour outliers up to 2051.
data_impact.indexes_relied_on: scans_cold PRIMARY KEY (org_id, scanned_at, kit_id, id) and PARTITION BY toYYYYMM(scanned_at) -- together these are the entire basis of the GO verdict. The idx_org_id set skip-index adds nothing once the primary key has already pruned.

resource_envelope.trigger: The spike's whole subject is a query class on a 2.18-billion-row ClickHouse table on a dashboard page-load path, multiplied by four new cards and by every viewing user.
resource_envelope.growth: scans_cold measured at 2,139,764,771 rows / 120.08 GiB when the ticket was written (2026-09-01) and 2,180,621,658 rows / 122.58 GiB on 2026-09-08 -- roughly +40.9M rows / +2.5 GiB per week, about +5.8M rows/day. The per-org window cost grows with that rate; the 13-month series cost grows fastest because it spans the most partitions.
resource_envelope.allocation_sketch: Per card, cold: single-window total 447 MB peak / 190 ms (org 469, last month); 13-month series 2.51 GB peak / 1,351 ms with FINAL, 2.44 GB / 1,102 ms without. Four unbatched cards concurrently: 243,048,568 rows read, 10.09 GB read, ~10.03 GB concurrent peak memory, slowest query 3.818 s (2.6x solo). Warm renders cost nothing (getMonthlyData caches per month per org). The rollup alternative is 234,054 rows / 51 MB / 17 ms for the same 13-month series.
